first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, which directly threatens both activation and early product adoption. Memory_31 showed signup simplification lifted first-week activation in SMB; memory_86 demonstrated that shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value. These are the most directly causally linked to our current problem. While competitor pricing pressure exists, activation degradation is the primary lever we can control quickly with high confidence. A standard experiment can validate whether simplified onboarding replicates prior gains and addresses the completion decline. This preserves focus on sustainable qualified revenue (not race-to-bottom pricing) and leaves referral incentive and enterprise sales paths as fallback options if this week's test shows insufficient lift.

final.rationale: Archive validation confirms both memories are reliable. Memory_31 (signup simplification) showed +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB with minimal retention risk (-1%). Memory_86 (shortened onboarding) showed +13% completion, -2.1 day time-to-value, and +3% retention. Our current 4% QoQ completion decline and 6% activation decline align directly with the problem space these interventions address. The verified retention uplift from shortened onboarding (+3%) further supports this choice. We run simplify_onboarding as a standard_experiment scaled to SMB and self-serve segments where prior evidence is strongest. This addresses the immediate activation and completion decline while preserving long-term qualified revenue focus and avoiding the margin risk of promotional pricing against a competitor. The experiment is executable this week and leaves enterprise_sales_assist available as a complementary lever if needed post-results.
